newsitem.title: USA: SEC acts against consultant concerning localities.
newsitem.headline: SEC acts against consultant concerning localities.

text.p: The SEC said on Monday that it filed administrative proceedings against a Houston financial consultant and one of his friends in connection with activities involving some Texas school districts and other public investors.
The Securities and Exchange Commission charged that the consultant, Russell William Stein, recommended that an investment adviser hire his friend, Ford Albritton, to help the adviser get clients.
The adviser paid Albritton and his firm, Dover and Associates, Inc. $641,000 to maintain client relationships with the five public investors, from January 1992 to May 1995, SEC alleged.
The SEC said Dover paid Stein's son $248,381 even though Albritton and his firm "performed no significant" services for the adviser to the school districts and other clients.

SEC said Stein failed to disclose to the public investors his financial connections to Albritton and to Stein's son. Stein also did not disclose that Allbritton got solicitation fees from the adviser and that Stein had a conflict of interest in advising the institutional investors, SEC charged.
SEC did not name the institutional investors.
Stein and Albritton were unavailable for comment.
